proof_summary: For Lemoine’s conjecture, an odd \(k>61\) is written as \(2n+1\), so the assumed representation immediately gives \(k=q+2p\), while the remaining odd values are handled by a finite check. For twin primes, if only finitely many admissible \(p\) existed, the Chinese remainder theorem would produce a sufficiently large odd \(M\) with \(M\equiv2p\pmod{\ell_p}\) for each of them, where \(\ell_p\) is the next indexed prime; the assumed decomposition would then make its prime remainder \(q=M-2p\) a proper multiple of \(\ell_p\), a contradiction, and injectively mapping the resulting infinitely many \(p\) to the indexed primes yields infinitely many prime pairs differing by two.
